newsitem.title: POLAND: Budimex to continue shift to domestic mkt.
newsitem.headline: Budimex to continue shift to domestic mkt.

text.p: Polish builder Budimex SA , which revised down its 1997 earnings forecast last week, plans to help make up the difference by further shifting activities to the home market, the firm's president said on Wednesday.

"To decrease losses we plan to increase sales in the domestic market. After the first half of 1997 the domestic market takes up 50 percent of our sales, and in 1998 it will be 60 to 70 percent," Grzegorz Tuderek told a news conference.
He said last year domestic operations made up 24 percent of Budimex sales.
Last Thursday the firm revised down its 1997 group pre-tax profit forecast to 23 million zlotys from 33.7 million and parent pre-tax to 15 million from 25.7 million.
Budimex revised down its 1997 group net profit forecast to 18 million zlotys from 28 million and parent net to 13 million from 23.5 million.

It said it was making the revision in part due to a downturn of the business cycle on the German and Czech markets, flooding in the Czech Republic and limited sales in the Commonwealth of Independent States.
It also said new regulations requiring foreign contractors active in Germany to bring wages to levels comparable with those in the European Union made its business less competitive.
Tuderek on Wednesday said Budimex had to make a 4.2 million zloty financial provision after one of its German clients went bankrupt while owing the Polish company that amount.
He said problems linked with Czech contracts lowered profit forecasts by about two million zlotys, in the CIS 4.8 million.
